nodes.description: Immutable address state variable set to msg.sender in the constructor; used as the sole access-control identity and as the payout recipient in withdraw.
Immutable IERC20 reference hardcoded to the mainnet WETH address 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2; never used in logic.
Public constant uint256 of 1000000000 ether that appears as a large allowance-like bait value; never used in logic.
Immutable hardcoded address 0xFd495eeEd737b002Ea62Cf0534e7707a9656ba19 used as bait; never used in logic.
Deployment-time constructor that assigns me = msg.sender, fixing the privileged withdraw address to the deployer.
Payable receive hook that accepts ether and allows the contract balance to be funded by any sender.
External function guarded by require(msg.sender == me) that forwards the entire contract balance to me through a low-level call.
Unrestricted external function that delegatecalls an attacker-supplied address with the finesse() selector, enabling arbitrary code execution in this contract's storage context.
Caller address supplied by the transaction; consumed by the constructor and as the only authorization check in withdraw.
Low-level delegatecall inside bait that executes attacker-controlled code at _pickpocket, allowing total takeover of the contract's storage and balance.
Low-level value call inside withdraw that sends address(this).balance to me before checking success, a state-changing external interaction that can reenter.
Caller-supplied address parameter of bait that becomes the delegatecall target for the finesse() payload.

edges.reason: msg.sender is assigned to the immutable state variable me during construction.
Entry into withdraw is gated only by require(msg.sender == me), so the caller identity fully determines the privileged path.
The unrestricted external function bait accepts an arbitrary caller-supplied address parameter _pickpocket.
The attacker-controlled parameter _pickpocket flows directly into the delegatecall target, allowing arbitrary external code to be executed.
Any caller can reach bait and therefore trigger the delegatecall, executing attacker-chosen code without authorization.
withdraw performs an external low-level value call to me, letting the recipient reenter the contract before completion.
State variable me supplies the destination of the balance transfer, so the recipient controls the external call.
msg.sender must equal me to pass the check, linking the untrusted caller to the reentrant low-level call.
withdraw reads the immutable state variable me for both the authorization check and the payout address.

normalization_plan.reason: Parameter _pickpocket is only meaningful as the attacker-controlled argument of bait; it is absorbed into the bait function node for normalization.
